concepts.name: NCBC powers, Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, language policy and the GST Council basics
concepts.description: The powers and constitutional status of the National Commission for Backward Classes, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities under Article 350B, the three-language formula, the classical languages, and the origin and composition of the GST Council.
concepts.idea: The NCBC, the Special Officer and the GST Council are constitutional bodies whose powers are investigative or recommendatory and whose composition, history and dates are the minute facts UPSC tests.
concepts.rule: The NCBC was set up in 1993 after the Mandal case, became a constitutional body under Article 338B by the 102nd Amendment (2018), and has civil-court powers for inquiry but is investigative and recommendatory, not a court. The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (Article 350B, 7th Amendment 1956, on the recommendation of the States Reorganisation Commission) is appointed by the President, investigates the safeguards of Articles 29, 30, 347 and 350A and reports to the President; the Constitution does not specify his tenure, qualifications or removal, and per Laxmikanth his headquarters is back at New Delhi since 2015. Classical-language status needs, among other things, early texts 1500-2000 years old; Tamil (2004), Sanskrit (2005), Telugu and Kannada (2008), Malayalam (2013), Odia (2014) and Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali (2024) have it. The GST Council (Article 279A, 101st Amendment, 2016) is chaired by the Union Finance Minister with the Union Minister of State for Revenue or Finance and one Minister from each State, the Union Revenue Secretary is its ex-officio Secretary and the CBIC Chairperson a non-voting invitee.
concepts.example: A report of the NCBC on a State matter goes to that State government for the legislature, while the Special Officer's reports go to the President for laying before Parliament.

questions.q: With reference to the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities provided for by Article 350B, which one of the following is laid down by the Constitution itself?
questions.a: That the Special Officer is to be appointed by the President
o: That the Special Officer is to be appointed by the President
The term of office of the Special Officer, which is fixed at five years
The qualifications that a person must hold to be appointed as Special Officer
The procedure by which the Special Officer may be removed from office
questions.e: Article 350B says the Special Officer is appointed by the President (not the Governor). The Constitution does not specify his qualifications, tenure, salary and allowances, service conditions or procedure for removal.
w: The Constitution leaves the tenure unspecified; the five-year figure is invented.
Qualifications are not specified in the Constitution.
The procedure for removal is not specified in the Constitution.

questions.q: The headquarters of the office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities) was set up in 1957 at New Delhi and was later shifted to Allahabad. What is its present position?
questions.a: It was shifted back to New Delhi in 2015
o: It was shifted back to New Delhi in 2015
It continues at Allahabad (Prayagraj), where it was shifted after 1957
It was shifted back to New Delhi in 2005
It was shifted back to New Delhi in 2021
questions.e: The office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was established in 1957 at New Delhi, was shifted to Allahabad after a brief period, and was shifted back to New Delhi in 2015. The Allahabad location was therefore only an interim one.
w: Allahabad was only the interim location; the headquarters has since been shifted back to New Delhi.
The shift back to New Delhi took place in 2015, not 2005.
The shift back to New Delhi took place in 2015, not 2021.

questions.q: The Goods and Services Tax Council has its Secretariat at New Delhi. Who acts as the ex-officio Secretary to the Council?
o: The Chairperson of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs
The Secretary of the Department of Expenditure
questions.e: The Union Revenue Secretary (Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance) is the ex-officio Secretary to the GST Council set up under Article 279A; the Secretariat is at New Delhi.

The CBIC Chairperson is a permanent non-voting invitee, not the Secretary.
The Council's Secretariat works under the Department of Revenue, not the Department of Expenditure.

questions.q: While investigating a matter or inquiring into a complaint, the National Commission for Backward Classes enjoys civil-court powers. Which one of the following best describes the nature of its powers?
questions.a: They are those of a civil court for specified matters, yet the Commission is an investigative and recommendatory body, not a court
o: They are those of a civil court for specified matters, yet the Commission is an investigative and recommendatory body, not a court
They are those of a High Court, including the power to punish persons for contempt of the Commission
They are limited to advising the Government, with no power to summon any person or examine anyone on oath
They are quasi-judicial powers whose orders bind both the Union and the State Governments
questions.e: The NCBC may summon and examine on oath, call for documents, receive evidence on affidavits, requisition public records and issue summons, and may exercise any other power the President determines. These powers are investigative and recommendatory: it cannot punish or issue binding orders, and it is not a court of law.
w: The Commission has civil-court powers, not those of a High Court, and cannot punish.
It does have power to summon any person from any part of India and examine on oath.
Its recommendations are not binding; it cannot issue binding orders.
tr: Civil-court powers are not a court

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC):

1. The Commission may regulate its own procedure, including the conduct of hearings, field visits and preparation of reports.
2. The Commission must take the approval of the Union Home Ministry before summoning a person who lives outside the State where the inquiry is held.
3. The Commission can requisition any public record from a court or an office and issue summons for the examination of witnesses and documents.
4. The Commission can require the discovery and production of any document.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The power to regulate its own procedure is expressly conferred. Statement 2 is incorrect: The Commission can summon any person from any part of India and examine him on oath; no such approval is needed. Statement 3 is correct: Both are among the civil-court powers listed. Statement 4 is correct: Requiring the discovery and production of any document is among its civil-court powers.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the origin and status of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC):

1. Following the Mandal case judgement of 1992, the Commission was first set up in 1993 as a statutory body to examine complaints of under-inclusion, over-inclusion or non-inclusion in the lists of backward classes.
2. Article 338-B, which made the Commission a constitutional body, came through the 102nd Amendment of 2018.
3. Article 342-A, inserted in 2018, empowers the NCBC itself to specify the socially and educationally backward classes of each State.
4. The National Commission for Backward Classes Act, 1993 was repealed in 2018 after the Commission became a constitutional body.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: following the Supreme Court direction in the Mandal case (1992), the Commission was first set up under the 1993 Act as a statutory body. Statement 2 is correct: Article 338-B was inserted by the 102nd Amendment (2018), making the Commission constitutional. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 342-A enables the President to specify the socially and educationally backward classes; the Commission does not. Statement 4 is correct: the 2018 Repeal Act repealed the 1993 Act.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct.
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct.
tr: President specifies the list, not the Commission

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions and reporting of the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC):

1. It participates and advises on the socio-economic development of the socially and educationally backward classes and evaluates their progress of development under the Union or a State.
2. It makes recommendations on the measures that the Union or a State should take for the effective implementation of the safeguards for these classes.
3. It presents its annual report to the Prime Minister, who has it laid before Parliament with a memorandum of action taken.
4. Its constitutional status is at par with that of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: advising on socio-economic development and evaluating progress is a listed function. Statement 2 is correct: recommending measures for effective implementation of safeguards is a listed function. Statement 3 is incorrect: the annual report goes to the President, who places it before Parliament with a memorandum of action taken. Statement 4 is correct: its constitutional status is at par with the NCSC and NCST.
w: '1, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 3, which is incorrect:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities:

1. The safeguards it examines include those in Articles 29, 30, 347 and 351.
2. It investigates all matters relating to the safeguards for linguistic minorities and reports to the President, who has the reports laid before Parliament and sent to the State governments concerned.
3. It monitors implementation on the ground through questionnaires to States and Union Territories, field visits to minority-dominated areas, and conferences and seminars.
4. Its function is judicial in character, so it can penalise officials who defy the safeguards.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 351 (development of the Hindi language) is not a minority safeguard; the fourth article examined is 350A on mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage. Statement 2 is correct: This is the duty given by Article 350B. Statement 3 is correct: These are the monitoring methods listed. Statement 4 is incorrect: The function is investigative and evaluative, not judicial or punitive, and the office has no binding powers.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the classical languages of India:

1. Tamil was declared a classical language in 2004 and Sanskrit in 2005.
2. Odia was declared a classical language before Malayalam.
3. Telugu and Kannada were declared classical languages in the same year, 2008.
4. Marathi and Gujarati were among the five languages added in 2024.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Tamil 2004 and Sanskrit 2005. Statement 2 is incorrect: Malayalam was declared in 2013 and Odia in 2014, so Odia came later. Statement 3 is correct: Both were declared in 2008. Statement 4 is incorrect: The 2024 additions were Marathi, Pali, Prakrit, Assamese and Bengali; Gujarati was not one of them.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about language policy and the three-language formula:

1. The three-language formula for the school system consists of English, Hindi and a regional language.
2. The formula is associated with the Kothari Commission as a compromise between national integration and linguistic diversity.
3. Tamil Nadu opposed the formula and teaches only English and Tamil in its educational institutions.
4. The Official Languages Act, 1963 introduced the three-language formula for school education.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the three-language formula for schools comprises English, Hindi and a regional language. Statement 2 is correct: the formula is widely associated with the Kothari Commission (1964-66) as a compromise between national integration and linguistic diversity. Statement 3 is correct: Tamil Nadu rejected the formula and teaches only Tamil and English. Statement 4 is incorrect: the Official Languages Act, 1963 provides for the continued use of English, in addition to Hindi, for Union official purposes even after 1965; it did not lay down school languages.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct.
tr: Formula attributed to a wrong enactment
Allocation of languages in the formula

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Goods and Services Tax (GST) Council:

1. It is a constitutional body constituted under Article 279A, inserted by the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
2. Its Vice-Chairperson is chosen from among themselves by the members of the Council from the States, who also decide his term.
3. The Chairperson of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs is a voting member of the Council.
4. The President's order constituting the Council was issued on 15 September 2017.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 279A and the 101st Amendment. Statement 2 is correct: the State members choose one of themselves as Vice-Chairperson and can decide his term. Statement 3 is incorrect: The CBIC Chairperson is a permanent invitee without a vote, by decision of the Union Cabinet. Statement 4 is incorrect: The President constituted the Council in 2016; the order was issued on 15 September 2016.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities:

1. The office was created in 1950 when the Constitution came into force.
2. The Special Officer is designated the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities and, at the Central level, falls under the Ministry of Minority Affairs.
3. Linguistic minorities are identified on an all-India basis as groups whose mother tongue is different from Hindi.
4. Article 350B is located in Part XVIII of the Constitution.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 350B was inserted by the 7th Amendment Act, 1956 and the office was created in 1957. Statement 2 is correct: Stated on. Statement 3 is incorrect: A linguistic minority is a group whose mother tongue differs from that of the majority in the State or part of a State, so minorities are determined state-wisefootnote 1). Statement 4 is incorrect: Article 350-B was inserted in Part XVII (Official Language); Part XVIII deals with Emergency Provisions.

'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities:

1. Article 350B was inserted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956 on the recommendation of the States Reorganisation Commission.
2. Its regional offices are at Belagavi, Chennai and Kolkata.
3. The Constitution fixes a five-year term of office for the Special Officer.
4. Its reports go to the President, who causes them to be laid before Parliament and sent to the State governments concerned.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 350B was inserted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956 on the recommendation of the States Reorganisation Commission. Statement 2 is correct:(Belgaum, Chennai, Kolkata, each under an Assistant Commissioner). Statement 3 is incorrect: The Constitution does not specify the tenure. Statement 4 is correct: summary table. So exactly 3 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 3 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the GST Council:

1. The Council has to establish a mechanism to adjudicate disputes about its recommendations or their implementation between the Centre and the States or among the States.
2. Its stated vision is to set the highest standards of co-operative federation, being the first constitutional federal body vested with powers on major GST decisions.
3. It recommends compensation to States for loss of revenue due to GST for a period of ten years.
4. An act of the Council becomes invalid if there is a vacancy or a defect in the constitution of the Council.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: The Council has to establish a mechanism to adjudicate disputes about its recommendations or their implementation between the Centre and the States or among the States. Statement 2 is correct:(calls it a model of cooperative federalism). Statement 3 is incorrect: The compensation period is five years. Statement 4 is incorrect: A vacancy, a defect in the appointment of a member or a procedural irregularity not affecting the merits does not invalidate its acts. So exactly 2 statement(s) are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the National Commission for Backward Classes (NCBC):

1. It inquires into specific complaints about deprivation of the rights and safeguards of the socially and educationally backward classes.
2. It may receive evidence on affidavits while investigating a matter.
3. Any additional power of the Commission is determined by Parliament by law, not by the President.
4. The Union and State Governments must consult the Commission on major policy matters affecting backward classes, and the 105th Amendment Act, 2021 relieved the State Governments of this duty altogether.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: inquiring into specific complaints is a listed function. Statement 2 is correct: receiving evidence on affidavits is among its civil-court powers. Statement 3 is incorrect: the 'any other matter' is whatever the President may determine. Statement 4 is incorrect: the 2021 amendment exempted States from consultation only for preparing and maintaining their own lists of backward classes. So exactly 2 statements are correct.
w: 'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'Only three' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
'None' miscounts: exactly 2 of the 4 statements are correct.
tr: 105th Amendment exemption is limited to lists

Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: A language whose earliest texts are only about 800 years old would fail the antiquity test for classical status.

questions.q:
Match the safeguards for linguistic minorities in List-I with their subject in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 29
B. Article 30
C. Article 347
D. Article 350A

List-II
1. Special provision about a language spoken by a section of the population of a State
2. Instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage

concepts.name: GST Council functions and voting, Inter-State Council and Zonal Councils
concepts.description: What the GST Council recommends and how it votes, the Inter-State Council under Article 263 (functions, composition, secretariat, Standing Committee) and the structure of the Zonal Councils.
concepts.idea: Coordination bodies between the Centre and States advise rather than decide, and their composition and voting rules are precise.
concepts.rule: The GST Council recommends the taxes to be subsumed, goods and services to be taxed or exempted, model laws, place-of-supply principles, the threshold limit, rates with floor bands, special rates for calamities and special provisions for eleven States; decisions need not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes, the Centre carrying one-third and the States together two-thirds, with a quorum of one-half. Article 263 contemplates an Inter-State Council to inquire into and advise on disputes, investigate and discuss subjects of common interest and recommend coordination; the present Council was set up by a Presidential Order of 1990 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation, with the Prime Minister as Chairman, and a Standing Committee since 1996 under the Home Minister. Its Secretariat (1991) has also served the Zonal Councils since 2011. The five Zonal Councils are statutory bodies under the States Reorganisation Act, 1956, with the Union Home Minister as common Chairman and Chief Ministers as Vice-Chairman by yearly rotation.
concepts.example: The Centre alone (one-third of the weight) cannot carry a GST Council decision, and nor can the States alone (two-thirds), because three-fourths is needed.

questions.q: Under Article 279A, a decision of the Goods and Services Tax Council is valid only if it secures
questions.a: not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present and voting, with the Centre's vote weighing one-third of the votes cast
o: not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present and voting, with the Centre's vote weighing one-third of the votes cast
not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present and voting, with the Centre's vote weighing two-thirds of the votes cast
not less than two-thirds of the weighted votes of members present and voting, with the Centre and the States weighing one-half each
a simple majority of members present and voting, with every State carrying a vote equal to that of the Centre
questions.e: Every decision needs a majority of not less than three-fourths of the weighted votes of members present and voting; the Centre's vote has a weightage of one-third and the votes of all States combined two-thirds. The quorum is one-half of the total members.
w: The weights are the other way round: the Centre has one-third, the States together two-thirds.
The threshold is three-fourths, not two-thirds, and the weights are one-third and two-thirds.
The Council does not decide by simple majority or by one State, one vote.

questions.q: The GST Council recommends the principles for apportionment of the GST levied on supplies in the course of inter-State trade or commerce. This apportionment is provided for in
questions.e: Article 269A deals with levy and apportionment of GST on inter-State supplies; the Council recommends the principles. Article 246A is the special provision on legislating for GST, and Article 279A creates the Council.
w: Article 246A is the legislative power over GST, not the apportionment of inter-State GST.
Article 279A constitutes the GST Council; the apportionment provision is another article.
Article 286 deals with restrictions on State taxes on sale or purchase outside the State (not GST apportionment).

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly describes how the present Inter-State Council came into being?
questions.a: By a Presidential Order of 1990 under Article 263, following the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation
o: By a Presidential Order of 1990 under Article 263, following the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation
By an Act of Parliament of 1990, following the Rajamannar Committee's recommendation
By a Constitution Amendment Act of 1990, following the Administrative Reforms Commission's recommendation
By a Cabinet resolution of 1990 under Article 74, following the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation
questions.e: The Council was set up in 1990 through a Presidential Order under Article 263 on the Sarkaria Commission's recommendation, by the V. P. Singh government. Article 263 only contemplates such a council; no Act or Amendment created it.
w: No Act of Parliament created it, and the Rajamannar report went to the Tamil Nadu Government in 1971.
No Constitution Amendment was needed; Article 263 already permits a council to be set up by the President.
It was set up by the Inter-State Council Order of 28 May 1990 under Article 263, not by a Cabinet resolution.

questions.q: Who is the common Chairman of the five Zonal Councils?
o: The Union Minister for Development of the North Eastern Region
A Chief Minister of one of the member States, by annual rotation
questions.e: The Union Home Minister is the common Chairman of all five Zonal Councils. The Chief Ministers of the member States serve as Vice-Chairman by rotation for one year at a time.
w: The Prime Minister chairs the Inter-State Council, not the Zonal Councils.
The DoNER Minister is the Vice-Chairman of the North Eastern Council, not Chairman of the Zonal Councils.
A Chief Minister serves as Vice-Chairman by rotation, not as Chairman.

questions.q: The Secretariat of the Inter-State Council performs several duties. Which one of the following is NOT a duty of the Secretariat?
questions.a: Adjudicating the disputes between States that are referred to the Council
o: Adjudicating the disputes between States that are referred to the Council
Organising the meetings of the Council
Preparing agenda notes and background papers for the Council
Following up on the decisions and recommendations of the Council
questions.e: The Secretariat organises meetings, prepares agenda notes and background papers, follows up decisions and recommendations and facilitates coordination between the Centre, States and Zonal Councils. Adjudication is not its task; even the Council only enquires into and advises upon disputes (Article 263(a)).
w: Organising meetings is a duty of the Secretariat.
Preparing agenda notes and background papers is a duty of the Secretariat.
Follow-up of decisions and recommendations is a duty of the Secretariat.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the functions of the GST Council:

1. It recommends the taxes, cesses and surcharges of the Union, the States and local bodies that are to be subsumed in GST.
2. It recommends the model GST laws, the principles of levy and the principles governing the place of supply.
3. It recommends the threshold limit of turnover below which goods and services may be exempted from GST.
4. It recommends the rate structure for GST, with floor rates and bands.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 279A(4) makes the Council recommend the taxes, cesses and surcharges of the Union, States and local bodies to be subsumed in GST. Statement 2 is correct: it recommends model GST laws, the principles of levy and the principles governing place of supply. Statement 3 is correct: it recommends the threshold limit of turnover below which goods and services may be exempted. Statement 4 is correct: it recommends the GST rates, including floor rates with bands.

Statement 3 is correct: Under Article 263(c), it can make recommendations on such a subject, particularly for the better coordination of policy and action. concepts.name: Zonal Council membership, North Eastern Council and committees on Centre-State relations
concepts.description: The membership of each Zonal Council, the North Eastern Council, the classification of Centre-State relations and the Rajamannar, Sarkaria and Punchhi reform recommendations.
concepts.idea: Each committee on Centre-State relations is tied to particular recommendations, and attributing one commission's demand to another is the standard trap.
concepts.rule: Northern (Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Delhi, Chandigarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Ladakh), Central (Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh), Eastern (Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal), Western (Goa, Gujarat, Maharashtra, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu) and Southern (Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Karnataka, Kerala, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry) are the Zonal Councils; the North Eastern Council has eight members, Sikkim added in 2002. The Rajamannar Committee (appointed by the Tamil Nadu Government in 1969) sought residuary powers for States, a permanent Inter-State Council, omission of Articles 356, 357 and 365 and abolition of the All-India Services. The Sarkaria Commission (1983-88, 247 recommendations) kept a strong Centre, wanted Article 356 as a last resort, strengthened All-India Services and a permanent Inter-State Council. The Punchhi Commission (2007-10) concluded that cooperative federalism is the key and sought fixed tenure for Governors and exceptional use of Article 356.
concepts.example: Abolishing the All-India Services is a Rajamannar demand; Sarkaria wanted them strengthened.

questions.q: Which one of the following correctly lists the States that make up the Central Zonal Council?
questions.a: Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh

Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Chhattisgarh, Himachal Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
Jharkhand, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh
questions.e: The Central Zonal Council covers Chhattisgarh, Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh; its headquarters is Prayagraj.

Jharkhand belongs to the Eastern Zonal Council.

questions.q: Since July 2018 the North Eastern Council has had the Union Home Minister as its ex-officio Chairman. Who is its ex-officio Vice-Chairman?
questions.a: The Union Minister in charge of the Ministry of Development of the North Eastern Region
o: The Union Minister in charge of the Ministry of Development of the North Eastern Region
The Governor of Assam, by rotation among the Governors of the member States
The Chief Minister of a member State, by annual rotation
questions.e: The Minister (In-charge) of the Ministry of DoNER is the ex-officio Vice-Chairman. Rotation by Chief Ministers is the Zonal Councils' arrangement for their Vice-Chairman.
w: The Vice-Chairman is not chosen by rotation among Governors.
Annual rotation of a Chief Minister is the pattern for the Zonal Councils, not the North Eastern Council.
A civil servant is not the Vice-Chairman; the post goes to the DoNER Minister.

questions.q: The Rajamannar Committee, which examined Centre-State relations and recommended utmost autonomy for the States, was appointed in 1969 by
o: the Union Government on the advice of the Planning Commission
questions.e: The Committee headed by Dr P. V. Rajamannar was appointed by the Tamil Nadu Government (the DMK government of the time); it had three members and submitted its report in 1971.
w: It was a State-appointed body, not a Union Government committee; the Centre ignored its report.
West Bengal's own memorandum came in 1977 and is a different exercise; the Rajamannar Committee was a Tamil Nadu body.
The Administrative Reforms Commission was a Union body of 1966 and a different exercise.

questions.q: The Central Government implemented 180 of the 247 recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission. Which one of the following is described as the most important recommendation implemented?
questions.a: The establishment of the Inter-State Council in 1990
o: The establishment of the Inter-State Council in 1990
The renaming of the National Development Council as the National Economic and Development Council
The prescription in the Constitution of consultation with the Chief Minister in the appointment of the Governor
The total omission of Articles 356, 357 and 365
questions.e: Of the 247 recommendations of the Sarkaria Commission, the Centre implemented 180; the most important one implemented was the establishment of the Inter-State Council in 1990 under Article 263. Omission of Articles 356, 357 and 365 was the Rajamannar Committee's demand, not Sarkaria's.
w: The renaming of the NDC remained only a recommendation; the Inter-State Council is the important one implemented.
Consulting the Chief Minister on the Governor's appointment remained only a recommendation; the Inter-State Council is the important one implemented.
That was a Rajamannar Committee demand, which the Centre ignored.

questions.q: Which principle did the Punchhi Commission conclude would be the key to sustaining India's unity, integrity and social and economic development?
questions.e: The Punchhi Commission (constituted 2007, report 2010) concluded that cooperative federalism would be the key to sustaining India's unity, integrity and social and economic development.
w: The Commission's conclusion was cooperative, not competitive, federalism.
Asymmetric federalism was not its conclusion.
A strong Centre was Sarkaria's theme; the Punchhi Commission's stated key is cooperative federalism.

concepts.name: Comparison of constitutional bodies: articles, appointment, tenure and removal
concepts.description: A cross-body comparison of the Articles, appointing authorities, tenures and removal of the Election Commission, CAG, Finance Commission, UPSC, SPSC, national commissions, Special Officer, GST Council and Inter-State Council.
concepts.idea: A table of Articles, appointers, age limits and removal procedures lets UPSC set elimination questions across bodies.
concepts.rule: Article 148 is the CAG, 263 the Inter-State Council, 279A the GST Council, 280 the Finance Commission, 315-323 the Public Service Commissions, 324 the Election Commission, 338 the NCSC, 338A the NCST, 338B the NCBC and 350B the Special Officer. The CEC and Election Commissioners are appointed by the President on a committee's recommendation under the 2023 Act and hold office for six years or until 65; the CAG and UPSC members also have six years or 65, SPSC members six years or 62. The CEC and CAG are removed like a Supreme Court judge, other Election Commissioners on the CEC's recommendation, and UPSC and SPSC members by the President after a Supreme Court inquiry for misbehaviour. The Finance Commission is constituted every fifth year or earlier and its members hold office as the President's order specifies; the GST Council and Inter-State Council are composed of office-holders.
concepts.example: A UPSC member appointed at 64 leaves at 65, while an SPSC member appointed at 62 would already have reached the age limit.
